items.title: EPSS Surge: CVE-2026-58644 (Microsoft SharePoint)
items.analysis: EPSS exploitation probability for CVE-2026-58644 surged from 0% to 46% (percentile 99%), indicating a significant increase in predicted or observed exploitation activity for this 2026-era vulnerability. It is not (yet) in CISA KEV — this signal typically precedes KEV listing and press coverage. Deserialization of untrusted data in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.
items.description: Deserialization of untrusted data in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

priority.reason: EPSS 46% probability of exploitation within 30 days. CVSS v3 base score 9.8.

impact.affected_versions: Microsoft SharePoint (specific versions not provided, assume all vulnerable until vendor clarifies)
impact.how_to_check: Inventory all Microsoft SharePoint installations and compare versions against the advisory. Review logs on matching hosts for unusual authentication or administrative actions.

w5h.upgrade_action: Apply current vendor patches for Microsoft SharePoint per the advisory
w5h.why_it_matters: This matters because EPSS puts exploitation probability at 46% within 30 days; critical severity means full compromise is likely if reached.

items.title: EPSS Surge: CVE-2014-0282
items.analysis: EPSS exploitation probability for CVE-2014-0282 surged from 47% to 51% (percentile 99%), indicating a significant increase in predicted or observed exploitation activity for this 2014-era vulnerability. It is not (yet) in CISA KEV — this signal typically precedes KEV listing and press coverage. Microsoft Internet Explorer 6 through 11 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted web site, aka "Internet Explorer Memory Corruption Vulnerability," a different vulnerability than CVE-2014-1775, CVE-2014-1779, CVE-2014-1799, CVE-2014-1803, and CVE-2014-2757.
